Multimodal fusion research package
Python · PyTorch · More · Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory · 2026 – present
A modular Python package for multimodal fusion experiments: configurable encoders, cross-attention bridges, evaluation metrics and reproducible pipelines. It includes a BLIP-2-inspired Q-Former bridge over Chemprop and ChemBERTa encoders, and attention-based analysis tools for identifying which structural and textual features contribute to a model’s predictions.

title: Differentiation and the Discrete Fourier Transform
text:
1 Background
There are plenty of ways to define the Fourier Transform, but here we’ll define the Fourier Transform of a function \(u\in L^2[0,2\pi]\) as \[\begin{align*}
\mathcal{F}[u](x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}\hat{u} e^{inx}\quad(\star)\\
\text{where}\ \hat{u}_n=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}u(x)e^{-inx}dx.
\end{align*}\] \(\mathcal{F}[u](x)\) is the Fourier Representation of \(u\), and \(\hat{u}_n\) are the Fourier coefficients. Our truncated Fourier Representation \(\mathcal{F}_N\) is defined as \[
\mathcal{F}_N[u](x)=\sum_{|n|\le N}\hat{u}_n e^{inx}.
\]

1.1 Quick Remarks:
If we define an inner product \(\inner{f}{g}:=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}f\bar{g}dx\), the set \(\{e^{inx}: n\in\mathbb{Z}\}\) is orthanormal with respect to the above inner product \[\begin{align*}
\inner{e^{imx}}{e^{inx}} &= \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} e^{i(m-n)x}\,dx
  = \frac{1}{2\pi i(m-n)} e^{i(m-n)x}\bigg|_0^{2\pi} = 0, \quad m\neq n, \\
\inner{e^{inx}}{e^{inx}} &= 1.
\end{align*}\] Notice \(\hat{u}_n = \inner{u}{e^{inx}}\), so each of our Fourier terms is a projection of \(u\) onto one of our basis funcitons, i.e. the Fourier basis.
By the completeness of \(L_2\) and the Fourier basis, we get the equality of \((\star)\).
We will show this some other time

title: Differentiation and the Discrete Fourier Transform
text:
2 Discritizaiton
Suppose we have a function \(f\) on the real interval \([0,2\pi]\), then we can discritize the interval with \(2N + 1\) points where \(x_j = j(\frac{2\pi}{2N+1})\) and \(j\in[2N]\). Additionally, we would like to interpolate the funciton values at each \(x_j\), i.e. \[
f(x_j)=\sum_{|k|\le N} \hat{f}_k e^{ikx_j}.
\] Let \(\mathbf E\) be a \((2N+1)\times (2N+1)\) matrix such that \((E)_{j m} = e^{ik x_j}\) where \(j\in[2N]\) corresponds to the row indices and \(m\in[2N]\) corresponds to column indices such that \(m=1\mapsto k= -N,\ \dots,\ m= 2N+1 \mapsto k=N\). Then let \(\mathbf{\hat{f}}=(\hat{f}_{-N},\dots, \hat{f}_N)^T\) and we can represent our interpolation scheme as \[
\mathbf E\mathbf{\hat{f}} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})
\] where \(\mathbf E\) is called the Fourier Matrix.

Theorem 1 . \(\mathbf E\) is orthoganal.


Proof. Let our discritizaiton scheme from above hold. We will show \(\mathbf E^* \mathbf E\) is a diagonal matrix. Let \((\mathbf E^*)_{\ell_1,:}\) denote a row of \(\mathbf E^*\) and \((\mathbf E)_{:, \ell_2}\) denote a column of \(\mathbf E\). Then, we have two cases.
\(Case \ 1:\ (\ell_1=\ell_2)\). \[\begin{align*}
(\mathbf E^* \mathbf E)_{\ell_1, \ell_1}
&= \sum_{j=0}^{2N}e^{-i\ell_1 x_j}e^{i\ell_2 x_j}\\
&= \sum_{j=0}^{2N}e^{i(-\ell_1+\ell_2)x_j} \\
&= \sum_{j=0}^{2N} 1 = 2N+1
\end{align*}\]
\(Case \ 2:\ (\ell_1\ne \ell_2)\) \[\begin{align*}
(\mathbf E^* \mathbf E)_{\ell_1, \ell_1}
&= \sum_{j=0}^{2N}e^{-i\ell_1 x_j}e^{i\ell_2 x_j}\\
&= \sum_{j=0}^{2N}e^{i(-\ell_1+\ell_2)x_j} \\
&= \sum_{j=0}^{2N}e^{i(-\ell_1+\ell_2)(\frac{2\pi}{2N+1})j}\\
&= \bigg(\frac{1-e^{i(\ell_2-\ell_1)2\pi}}{1-e^{i(-\ell_1+\ell_2)(\frac{2\pi}{2N+1})}}   \bigg)=0
\end{align*}\] since \[
|e^{i(-\ell_1+\ell_2)(\frac{2\pi}{2N+1})}|< 1\quad\text{and}\quad e^{i(\ell_2-\ell_1)2\pi}=1.
\] Hence \(\mathbf E^* \mathbf E=\frac{1}{2N+1}\mathbf I\).


Corollary 1 (Discrete Fourier Transform) The Discrete Fourier Transform is given by \[
\hat f_k = \frac{1}{2N+1}\sum_{j=0}^{2N} f(x_j)e^{-ikx_j}
\]


Proof. Let \(\mathbf E \mathbf{\hat f} = \mathbf f\). Multiplying by \(\mathbf E^*\) on the left yeilds, \[\begin{align*}
\mathbf E^* \mathbf E \mathbf{\hat f}&=\mathbf E^* \mathbf f\\
\mathbf{\hat f}&=\frac{1}{2N+1}\mathbf E^* \mathbf f
\end{align*}\] which implies the corollary above.

title: Differentiation and the Discrete Fourier Transform
text:
3 Differentiation
In the computational setting differential operators get discritized, i.e. they become matrices. Lets consider a discritizaiton with \(N\) points and \(f\) as above \[\begin{align*}
f(x)&\approx \sum_{n\in S_n}\hat{f}_n e^{inx}& S_n=\begin{cases}-\frac{N}{2},\dots,\frac{N}{2}-1&if\ N\ even\\ -\frac{N-1}{2},\dots,\frac{N-1}{2}&if \ N\ odd\end{cases}\\
\hat{f}_n&=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} f(x_j)e^{-inx_j}&x_j = j\frac{2\pi}{N}.
\end{align*}\] Then \[
\mathbf D_N^{m}f(x_j)\approx \sum_{n\in S_n}\hat{f}_n (in)^m e^{inx},
\] which can be represented as matrix vector multiplicaiton \[\begin{align*}
\mathbf D_N^{m}\mathbf f
&\approx\frac{1}{\sqrt N}\mathbf E\mathrm{diag}((in)^m, \dots, (in)^m)\mathbf{\hat f}\\
&=\frac{1}{N}\mathbf E\ \mathbf{\mathrm{diag}}((in)^m, \dots, (in)^m)\ \mathbf E^*\mathbf f
\end{align*}\] by Corollary 1. Then we get \(\mathbf D_N^{m}=\frac{1}{N}\mathbf E\ \mathbf{\mathrm{diag}}((in)^m, \dots, (in)^m)\ \mathbf E^*\), which is the eigen-decomposition of \(\mathbf D_N^{m}\) in the Fourier basis.
Notice the eigenvalue of \(\mathbf D_N^{m}\) are real and negative when \(m\) is even and strictly imaginary when \(m\) is odd.
crumbs: Differentiation and the Discrete Fourier Transform

title: Differentiation and the Discrete Fourier Transform
text:
4 PDEs
Consider the 1-D transport equation \(u_t=u_{x}\), then by discritizing the PDE we get \[
\frac{d}{dt}\overrightarrow{u}(t)=\mathbf D_N\overrightarrow{u}(t).
\] Indeed \(\mathbf D_N\) has complex eigenvalues in the Fourier basis. Further, \[\begin{align*}
\mathbf D_N \mathbf D_N^*
&=\frac{1}{N^2}\mathbf E\ \mathbf{\mathrm{diag}}((in)^m, \dots, (in)^m)\ \mathbf E^*(\mathbf E\ \mathbf{\mathrm{diag}}((in)^m, \dots, (in)^m)\ \mathbf E^*)^*\\
&=\mathbf I
\end{align*}\] so let \(\mathbf x, \mathbf y\in\mathbb{R}^N\), then \(\|\mathbf D_N \mathbf x -\mathbf D_N \mathbf y\|=\|\mathbf D_N(\mathbf x-\mathbf y)\|=\|\mathbf x-\mathbf y\|\). Hence, as an operator \(\mathbf D_N\) preserves rigid motions in euclidian space, as expected by the transport equation.
Now consider the 1-D diffusion equation \(u_t=u_{xx}\), then by discritizing the PDE we get \[
\frac{d}{dt}\overrightarrow{u}(t)=\mathbf D^2_N\overrightarrow{u}(t).
\] Since \(\mathbf D^2_N\) has real negative eigenvalues, from the ODE perspective we can think of the PDE as decaying to a fixed point in the Fourier basis, i.e. the \(k=0\) wavenumber.

title: Research
text:
Computational mathematics
Building computation around questions.
A recurring motif in my research is finding a problem and turning it into a mathematical question. Then, finding/creating a computational implimentation that can be run, checked and reproduced: a modular Python package for multimodal fusion experiments on molecular data, systems of ODEs solved and swept in Mathematica and MATLAB, and experiment pipelines that compare networks of LLM agents with a single-agent baseline.

Multimodal fusion for molecular property prediction
June 2026 – present · Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory · PI: Talita Perciano
A modular research package for multimodal fusion, with configurable encoders, cross-attention bridges, evaluation metrics and reproducible pipelines. I built a Q-Former bridge inspired by BLIP-2(vision language architecture) that combined Chemprop (GNN) and ChemBERTa (text) encoders to study molecular property prediction. The architecture is being extended for a DOE Genesis Mission collaboration with Berkeley, Cornell and LBNL focused on interpretable catalyst discovery.
Software


Complexity in multi-agent LLM networks
Fall 2023 – May 2025 · Arizona State University · with Dr. Joel Nishimura
This project tested the hypothesis that generative output from networks of LLM agents can be more complex, interesting and useful than the output of a single agent such as ChatGPT. It adapted established multi-agent implementations (Swarm, ChatDev, CAMEL) to specific contexts and scenarios, and introduced ChatScript, a multi-agent paradigm that models a media production company and writing room. Preliminary findings supported the hypothesis.
Manuscript in preparation · Presentations · ChatScript

title: Research
text:
Analysis
Playing with infinity.
Once a model is written down, the questions become what can be measured or proved about it: how its behavior depends on its parameters, and what a control can change. Analysis helps me understand convergence, approximation, and look into other toolsets like probability.

Population dynamics of gestational diabetes
June 2024 – present · MSRI-UP, Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute · with Alex Gaither and Javier Garcia Espinoza
A new population-level model of gestational diabetes, developed at MSRI-UP 2024 (theme: Mathematical Endocrinology) from a review of the literature: a system of ODEs for transitions between healthy, gestational diabetic and type 2 diabetic states. Analysis of the model uses parameter sweeps, sensitivity analysis and optimal control to evaluate the effects of interventions, in Mathematica and MATLAB.
Manuscript in preparation · 5 presentations


Representation geometry and fusion gains
June 2026 – present · Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
Part of the multimodal fusion project: evaluating whether the Gromov–Wasserstein distance between encoders predicts downstream fusion gains, across synthetic encoder regimes that separate redundant, complementary and degenerate information sources.
